mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over the next month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns within the following 20-day window.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of similar rising-rate regimes, or the FEDFUNDS increase is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests, or 60-day forward returns do not exceed the 10th percentile of similar labor strength episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.2% suggests accelerating demand growth, which elevates expected future corporate profits and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of months with similar demand growth signals.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in inventory levels (implied via supply chain stress indicators not in the catalog) predicts a supply-side shock that depresses equity valuations, yielding negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative returns in out-of-sample supply shocks, or INDPRO declines are not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the 3-month moving average of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 4% creates a discounting effect that increases the present value of future equities, producing positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero in a 95% confidence interval during easing phases.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (implied via labor market tightness not directly observable in the catalog) coinciding with a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) triggers optimism about absorption capacity, driving positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% in a single month following a rising job openings trend (implied from labor market context)
failure_condition: The effect is not detectable in the 60-day window (p > 0.05) or the correlation with 60-day returns is weak (R^2 < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of accelerating consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3% suggest policy tightening and eroded purchasing power, which tends to depress equity valuations and produce negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases at a CAGR > 0.3% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in 60% or more of similar inflation acceleration episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a high-unemployment, low-growth macro environment (UNRATE > 7% and INDPRO < 50) is associated with a 20-day S&P 500 forward return that is on average negative, regardless of other signals.
candidate_trigger: regime condition: UNRATE > 7% AND INDPRO < 50 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In the specified regime, 20-day forward returns are non-negative in more than 50% of instances.
